key_insight: MicroSyn-X generates realistic, diverse synthetic X‑ray sequences so deep networks can learn robust tracking and closed‑loop control of miniature medical devices without large clinical X‑ray datasets, enabling reliable sim‑to‑real transfer for robotic navigation.
problem_solved: Severe shortage of annotated X‑ray data and large domain gaps between limited clinical images and real surgical variability make it hard to train and validate AI trackers and controllers for tiny intrabody devices.
method: Physics‑aware synthetic X‑ray pipeline: render X‑rays from CT/anatomical models with instrument geometry and realistic imaging artifacts.
Domain randomization and noise modeling: vary anatomy, pose, contrast, motion, and acquisition parameters to cover surgical variability.
Train deep learning trackers and closed‑loop controllers on synthetic data, then validate and deploy with sim‑to‑real strategies for real‑time robotic navigation.
impact: Enables AI/ML teams to build and benchmark robust tracking and control systems for miniature medical devices without expensive clinical data collection, accelerating safe robot‑assisted interventions and reproducible research.

paper_title: Synthetic X‑ray‑driven tracking and control of miniature medical devices
